in_text_mentions: As demonstrated in Fig. 2, axial cranial computed tomography revealed a hypodense intracerebral lesion accompanied by extensive perifocal vasogenic edema and associated mass effect, radiologically consistent with a fungal cerebral abscess. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Case report of subcutaneous phaeohyphomycosis due to Pyrenochaeta romeroi; axial T1 MRI of the patient's foot demonstrates the subcutaneous fungal mass (ovoid subcutaneous nodule), a supported manifestation of the target disease. panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of the patient's lower legs from a case report of ruxolitinib-associated phaeohyphomycosis. The image shows an erythematous, swollen pre-tibial leg corresponding to the in-text description of a palpable fluid-filled collection that was aspirated for culture (Figure 1), supporting a subcutaneous cystic/nodular manifestation of phaeohyphomycosis. The diffuse cellulitis-like appearance is an atypical rather than classic nodular presentation.
